title: CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Every component f_i is convex on E; the regularizer r is strongly convex, so F(x)=n⁻¹∑ᵢf_i(x)+r(x) is convex.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The regularizer r is μ-strongly convex on all of E, with μ>0; consequently the composite objective is μ-strongly convex.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible, StrongConvexOn univ p.μ inst.regularizer.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: A differentiable smooth finite-sum term is added to a real-valued regularizer whose exact proximal minimizers are available; no smoothness of the regularizer is required.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The smooth term is the average of n≥1 convex components, each with an L-Lipschitz gradient, where L>0.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query selects any index i and point x and returns exactly ∇f_i(x), independently of the call index and oracle seed. There is no oracle noise or restriction to random index selection.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: For any a>0 and z,g∈E, the oracle returns an exact global minimizer of ‖v−z‖²/(2a)+⟪g,v−z⟫+r(v). Each proximal query counts as one oracle call, as does each component-gradient query.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean: Query.prox and spec.admissible proximal conditions; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space with a measurable-space structure; finite dimensionality is not assumed. All parameters E,n,L,μ,Δ,ε,x0 are public, with n≥1, L>0, μ>0, Δ≥0, ε>0. The components, regularizer, and proximal map are hidden instance data. A minimizer x* exists with F(x0)−F(x*)≤Δ. Smoothness is componentwise rather than merely average smoothness.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex.lean: Params, Instance, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a measurable E-valued random point. For some global minimizer x*, its objective gap is integrable and has integral at most ε; no distance or gradient-norm criterion is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is E[F(output)−F(x*)]≤ε under the product of algorithm and oracle seed laws. The oracle budget is fixed and holds for every seed; accuracy is required only in expectation.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard strongly convex composite finite-sum minimization formulation with exact component gradients, exact proximal access, known parameters, and expected objective-gap accuracy, stated over a real Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Strongly Convex Composite Finite Sums

We minimize F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x)+r(x) on a real Hilbert space E, where n≥1, the functions fi:E→R are convex with L-Lipschitz gradients, and r:E→R is μ-strongly convex, with L,μ>0. A given point x0∈E satisfies F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ for a global minimizer x⋆ and Δ≥0. The oracle returns component gradients and exact proximal minimizers of r. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap and EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈EF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ on E, which is equipped with a measurable structure. The algorithm receives E, n, L, μ, Δ, ε, and x0; the component functions and regularizer are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convex smooth components). Each fi is Fréchet differentiable on E. For every i∈{1,…,n}, x,y∈E, and t∈[0,1], fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y),∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Strongly convex regularizer and proximal access). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], r((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)r(x)+tr(y)−μ2t(1−t)∥x−y∥2. There is a map p:R×E×E→E such that, for every a>0 and z,g∈E, p(a,z,g)∈argminv∈E{∥v−z∥22a+⟨g,v−z⟩+r(v)}.

Assumption 3 (Initial objective gap). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈E,F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ.

A component-gradient query specifies i∈{1,…,n} and x∈E; the oracle returns ∇fi(x) at x. A proximal query specifies a∈R and z,g∈E; the oracle returns p(a,z,g). Its minimization property is required only for a>0. Each query of either kind counts as one call toward a shared oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space, minimize F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x)+ψ(x), with n≥1, convex differentiable L-smooth components, and an everywhere finite μ-strongly convex regularizer. Exact component gradients and exact proximal minimizers are available. Assume L,μ,ε>0, Δ≥0, and a minimizer x⋆ with F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ. Target: ∫[F(x^(ω))−F(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, where P is the algorithm’s random-sampling law.

Abbr: n: component count; L: component-gradient Lipschitz constant; μ: regularizer strong-convexity modulus; Δ: initial-gap bound; ε: target expected gap. Costs count component-gradient and proximal calls in total, including full-gradient refreshes; log is natural logarithm.

import LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Strong

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  n : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero n]
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.nonzero

inductive Query (p : Params) where
  | gradient (i : Fin p.n) (x : p.E)
  | prox (a : ℝ) (z g : p.E)

structure Instance (p : Params) where
  components : Fin p.n → p.E → ℝ
  regularizer : p.E → ℝ
  prox : ℝ → p.E → p.E → p.E

noncomputable def objective (p : Params) (inst : Instance p) (x : p.E) : ℝ :=
  LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective inst.components x + inst.regularizer x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Query
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p inst oracle :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ univ (inst.components i)) ∧
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (inst.components i) (gradient (inst.components i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ i x y, ‖gradient (inst.components i) x - gradient (inst.components i) y‖ ≤
      p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    StrongConvexOn univ p.μ inst.regularizer ∧
    (∀ a, 0 < a → ∀ z g, IsMinOn
      (fun v => ‖v - z‖ ^ 2 / (2 * a) + ⟪g, v - z⟫ + inst.regularizer v)
      univ (inst.prox a z g)) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x, oracle.answer k (0, (.gradient i x)) seed = gradient (inst.components i) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed a z g, oracle.answer k (0, (.prox a z g)) seed = inst.prox a z g) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective p inst) univ xstar ∧
      objective p inst p.x0 - objective p inst xstar ≤ p.Δ)
  successful p inst output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective p inst) univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective p inst (output ω) - objective p inst xstar)
        (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective p inst (output ω) - objective p inst xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.CompositeFiniteSumStronglyConvex
